claims.text: The trip_record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00108, and the trace's first fix (2026-07-20T07:19:20+08:00) matches the trip_record's started_at to the second, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) — that the artifacts describe the same trip — is met on the face of the bundle and not in dispute.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes at a 10-second sample interval over 100% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so it triggers none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07, and the excess measured from it therefore requires no independent corroboration under POL-RD-08(b).

Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 26.17 km on this trace — and the 26.2 km carried on the trip_record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, which the clause forbids citing for the threshold test. The rider relies on the trace figure, and the two agree to 30 metres, so nothing turns on the difference.

On the platform's own derived figures the trace exceeds the booking-time platform route estimate of 21.0 km by 5.17 km, which is 24.62% of the optimal — above the 0.8 km absolute limb and above the 20% proportional limb — and the derived deviation block records the status as 'established'; both establishment limbs of POL-RD-01 are therefore satisfied on the platform's own computation.

The fare breakdown charges the rider for 26.2 km at 0.75/km and 34.0 minutes at 0.28/min on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEX, so the whole of the excess trace distance was billed to her as distance and as time; that is the quantum POL-RD-02 exists to recompute, and the recomputation is arithmetic, not discretionary.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so POL-RD-03 exonerates not a metre — there is no named road, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km on which to run its cap formula. The rider cites the absence itself, which is a legitimate argument on this bundle.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver on this record: both rider messages carry waypoint_hint null and neither names a road, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run. By the clause's own terms the test is undecidable, no detour is exonerated under POL-RD-04, and the case falls to be decided on the remaining clauses — the driver's general assertion that he 'drove exactly where the app told me' is not a rider instruction to detour.

The two endpoint amendments explain only the 3.60 km difference between the booking-time estimate (21.0 km) and the platform's re-quote (24.60 km); the remaining 1.57 km by which the trace exceeds the re-quote is terminal routing, not relocation. The trace shows the T1 approach and then two loops of the T3 departure kerb inside 380 m of the amended pin, and the driver concedes in his own statement that he 'went round the loop twice'. POL-RD-05 excludes circling from excess only on the predicate that the rider was not at the amended point, and nothing on this record establishes that predicate: the amended dropoff carries no venue_id and no rider message places her anywhere but the terminal she asked for. POL-RD-05 licenses PARTIAL_REFUND as well as NO_ACTION, and the rider submits the 1.57 km residue — including the admitted looping — should be refunded rather than written off; if the tribunal instead holds that no deviation survives the re-quote, it should say expressly that the re-quote, and not the trace, is what defeated the claim.

The rider is not the serial claimant POL-RD-08's corroboration add-on is aimed at: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4 the clause names, so the extra corroboration requirement is not engaged and may not be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven; every other field on her profile is context only under POL-GEN-01.

Neither alternative fare regime closes the distance-refund route: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply, and trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not displace the solo optimal with a matched-itinerary baseline. The metered card is the only fare model in play.

If the deviation stands, POL-RD-02 fixes the remedy arithmetically: on the METERED card, with surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown (the trip_record carries no such field), recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 surcharge + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 27.63. Charged_total is 33.77, so the refund is 6.14, rounded up to SGD 6.15 — which is the arithmetic behind the rider's complaint that this trip usually costs her 'about $28'.

claims.text: Both endpoints of this trip were amended after booking: the rider moved the pin to Punggol MRT at 07:12:30 (trip_record.pickup_amended_at) and, in the chat at 07:41:40, asked to change the destination to Terminal 3 rather than Terminal 1, which the trip record shows was amended at 07:41:52. Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 baseline for this dispute is therefore the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints - the stored figure amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0 - and not the 21.0 km booked optimal. That re-quote is a stored field and is not to be re-derived by the tribunal.

The rider's 21 km figure, and the trip record's 24.8% deviation_pct, are both measured against the pre-amendment booked optimal of 21.0 km, and both are superseded by the amendment. The derived deviation block on the GPS trace makes the same error: its 5.17 km / 24.62% excess is computed against optimal_distance_km 21.0, the booked figure, so it does not answer the POL-RD-05 question either. On an amended trip the only comparison the policy permits is trace distance against 24.60 km.

Run that comparison and no deviation is established. The governing trace distance is 26.17 km against an amended optimal of 24.60 km - an excess of 1.57 km, or 6.4% of the amended optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass: an excess greater than 20% of optimal (4.92 km on this baseline) AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. 6.4% is nowhere near 20%, so the establishment test fails and no deviation exists on this trip.

The distance figure that governs is the trace itself, 26.17 km. POL-RD-01 states that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree the trace governs, and that the 26.2 km carried on the trip record and billed on the fare breakdown is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement which may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The distinction is small in this case, but it is what makes the comparison safe.

The trace runs the whole trip from 07:19:20, so its 26.17 km includes the Terminal 1 approach driven BEFORE the dropoff was amended at 07:41:52. POL-RD-05 provides that distance driven before an amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver. The 1.57 km residual therefore overstates the excess rather than understates it, and what is left cannot approach the 4.92 km the 20% gate requires.

The 'five minutes driving around the airport' is the T3 kerb loop the rider herself caused. The chat log records her request to change to T3 at 07:41:40 and the trip record the dropoff amendment at 07:41:52; the admissibility assessment of the GPS trace records two loops of the T3 departure kerb well inside 380 m of the amended pin, which is what a driver looking for a rider who is not at the kerb does. POL-RD-05 excludes from excess the circling within 400 m of an amended point where the rider was not present, and in any event the whole excess on the amended baseline is only 1.57 km.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09. The fare reconciles to the cent: 3.80 base + 19.65 distance + 9.52 time + 0.80 platform fee = 33.77, with no ERP lines, no surge, no promo discount and no waiting-time fee, and the airport surcharge is correctly 0.00 because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there. Every charge line has a counterpart on the trace, so no standalone pass-through correction is due.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged limb (b) of it: the excess she asserts is measured against the booked optimal that the amendment displaced, and measured against the amended optimal no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold can be shown. Nothing therefore shifts to the driver, and he is not required to invoke any exculpatory clause at all.

The POL-RD-06 profile check clears the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 402, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, and in any event the excess on this trip never reaches MATERIAL because it fails the establishment gate first. No conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) and no remedy uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available on this record.

No traffic advisory is in the pool: EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has weight_multiplier 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver does not invoke POL-RD-03 and asserts no road closure, and none is needed: this case is decided on POL-RD-05, whose re-quote is already stored on the trip record rather than being reconstructed from an advisory.

The outcome follows from the record. The dispute was filed by the rider, the fare breakdown stands at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence once the amended baseline is applied. Under POL-GEN-03 that is NO_ACTION: the present state stands and the charge is left exactly as it is.

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: NO_ACTION. The SGD 33.77 charge stands as it is; the fare breakdown is left at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

To the rider. Your receipt distance of 26.2 km looked wrong against the 21 km you usually see, and I accept the three artifacts describe the same trip (trip_id TRP-00108, trace starting 07:19:20 matching the trip record). But both ends of this trip changed after booking. You moved the pickup to Punggol MRT yourself (chat 07:11:58, pin amended 07:12:30) and at 07:41:40 you asked to switch the drop from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3, which the record shows was amended at 07:41:52. When the endpoints change, POL-RD-05 requires the deviation test to be re-run against the platform's re-quoted optimal route between the amended points, and that figure is stored on the trip record: amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km. It is not for me to re-derive it. That re-quote already absorbs the Punggol pickup and the T3 drop. Against 24.60 km, the governing trace distance of 26.17 km is an excess of 1.57 km, or 6.4%. POL-RD-01 sets a single gate: an excess counts as a deviation only if it exceeds 20% of the optimal route (4.92 km here) AND 0.8 km absolute. 6.4% is far below 20%, so no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 says the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, save for a billing-integrity correction. The 26.2 km on your receipt is the actual distance driven, and a metered fare charges that; the small margin over the best route is exactly the tolerance the threshold exists to leave alone. The 24.8% deviation_pct on the trip record and the 5.17 km / 24.62% excess in the GPS derived block are both computed against the pre-amendment 21.0 km estimate and are superseded by the amendments — they cannot be used. Your $6.15 POL-RD-02 recomputation does not run, because POL-RD-02 applies only once a deviation is established, and none is. Your point that the driver admitted going round the loop twice does not change this: the T3 kerb loop followed your own terminal change, and even taken in full the excess over the amended optimal is about 1.57 km, far short of the gate. On your profile, deviation_claims_60d is 1, so the extra-corroboration add-on in POL-RD-08 is not engaged; that finding makes no difference here because the claim fails on the baseline, not on credibility. Neither alternative fare regime applies: the fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null (so not POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (so not POL-RD-12).

To the driver. Your account is borne out by the record. The POL-RD-05 baseline is the amended re-quote (24.60 km / 31.0 min), the trace governs at 26.17 km, and the 1.57 km / 6.4% excess fails the POL-RD-01 establishment gate, so no deviation exists and your route is not penalised. No falsification of the amendment is possible: both amendment timestamps and both stored re-quote fields are present and non-null. Distance driven before the 07:41:52 drop amendment is not counted against you, and the T3 circling is at worst excluded under POL-RD-05 and at best immaterial to the gate either way. The POL-RD-06 profile check clears you: deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 402, no pattern is established, and since no deviation is established there is no MATERIAL finding, so neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No traffic advisory is invoked (EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and nothing is decided on POL-RD-03.

On the money and integrity. The fare reconciles to the cent (3.80 + 19.65 + 9.52 + 0.80 = 33.77), there are no ERP or toll lines, and the airport surcharge of 0.00 is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there (POL-RD-09(4) therefore produces no correction and no referral). No fare line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. There is no distance shortfall favouring the driver (billed 26.2 km vs trace 26.17 km), so no POL-RD-04 driver compensation is due.

On escalation. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so it triggers none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, timestamps do not disagree by more than 10 minutes or run backwards, and the refund does not exceed SGD 150.00. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The deciding facts are carried by the trip record and the GPS trace, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence in this ruling is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor.
